title: Eyetracking F-pattern on text and image-based pages
statement:
In an eyetracking study on an e-commerce site, the F-pattern was confirmed on text-based pages for both browsing and searching, while image-based pages produced a fairly uniform scan path with fixations on images dropping sharply near and below the fold, so the most important image-led content should sit at or above the fold.

Options:
- Text sections built for F-scanning: Text-heavy sections formatted for F-scanning: front-loaded copy with clear headings (fits: editorial, clear, professional)
- Key image above the fold: Image-led sections (product grids, feature visuals) with the most important image at or above the fold (fits: visual, retail, bold)
- Priority items in top rows: Long image grids with the highest-priority items in the top rows, since fixations drop sharply near and below the fold (fits: retail, practical, organized)
- Support searchers with clear labelling: Clear category labels and navigation for goal-directed visitors, who used unique scan paths on image-based pages (fits: practical, clear, friendly)

source.title: "F" Pattern Scanning of Text and Images in Web Pages
source.authors: Sav Shrestha; Kelsi Lenz; Justin Owens; Barbara Chaparro
source.venue: 51st Annual Meeting of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society (HFES), Baltimore
